top_story: Israel’s war and displacement regime in Gaza entered a harsher winter phase on 8-9 November, as the first major rains flooded tent encampments, wrecked about 70,000 shelters, and pushed already strained rescue crews into maximum emergency. The danger turned immediately lethal on 9 November when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents, killing a woman and three young children and exposing how exposure, weak shelter, and repeated displacement now magnify ordinary weather into mass civilian risk. In the West Bank, the 7 November violent seizure and occupation of Palestinian homes by Israeli settlers in Jericho points to a parallel escalation in coercive pressure on Palestinian communities outside Gaza. Taken together, these developments show a widening landscape of Palestinian insecurity in which direct violence, dispossession, and infrastructural collapse reinforce each other across different arenas.
